title: 2024 budget service expansions and capital program
subtitle: Staffing requests, lobbyist registry, LRT service levels, capital timing, and new provincial and federal funding cuts
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee reviewed the 2024 plan and budget under the "resilient and future ready organization" theme and recommended several staff-related service expansions for the 2024 operating budget. These cover labour relations, disability and return-to-work support, AI-enabled service delivery, a lobbyist registry, and two data positions. Votes ranged from lopsided to close on the data analyst position {{vote:m3}}.

On capital, the committee recommended moving about $37.6 million of planned 2024 spending into 2025 and 2026 to better match what staff expect to complete {{vote:m5}}. It also recommended improving Light Rail Transit service, with 10-minute peak frequency from June 2024 {{vote:m6}}.

Staff reported that assessment growth of 2.18% has been confirmed, and the budget impact currently stands at 8%. Staff also said that new provincial and federal notices cut homelessness and children's services funding. Councillors asked staff to report back on December 13, when budget day is scheduled, on delaying hiring start dates to lower the 2024 levy. These recommendations go to Council for final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended including service expansions for a Labour Relations Advisor, short-term disability and WSIB disability advisors, and AI-enabled service delivery in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended including a service expansion for a Lobbyist Registry in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended including a Data Insights Analyst service expansion in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended including a Service Transformation Data Specialist expansion in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended amending the preliminary capital program as shown on slides 18 to 20, mostly shifting 2024 spending into 2025 and 2026 {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended amending the LRT service expansion to 10-minute peak headways all year from June 2024, keeping 15-minute shoulder-period headways {{vote:m6}}.

debate: Some councillors questioned why more staff were being requested in a hard year for taxpayers. They asked whether existing positions could be repurposed or some work paused, and asked for comparisons with other regions rather than area municipalities. Staff said repurposing happens continuously and that most additions are tied to service expansions.

Staff said the disability advisors should shorten absences and cut replacement and overtime costs. A senior staff member said water and wastewater operators are hard to replace, so absences reduce preventive maintenance. One councillor asked how those savings show up in the budget, and staff said no offsetting reduction was made.

Councillors discussed delaying new-position start dates to reduce the 2024 levy. Staff noted this would raise the cost in 2025, and some positions are fully funded by other governments or tied to service changes. Staff were asked to report back on start dates for December 13.

Supporters of the data positions said the region has collected data without enough capacity to analyse it. They said analysis would inform asset management and traffic decisions. Councillors asked how many analysts the region has and whether the two roles overlap.

Some councillors raised concern about road widening spending given climate goals. Staff said projects follow the master plan and emphasize active transportation. Councillors also criticized the new federal and provincial funding reductions and called for advocacy for a new fiscal deal.
